rulings.ruling: Ruling: finding; the open difference is representation and the line carries a project defect. (1) executable-triage-v1 (triage/eic.json; 1,083 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 134 partial records; 1,717 comparisons): 0 differ, 1,717 agree; the candidate's extra scope.schedule1 branch reaches Worksheet B only on returns the project refuses on that screen (see eic.self_employed). (2) Project, finding: i1040gi p. 43, Step 6: "1. Do you want the IRS to figure the credit for you? ... No. Go to Worksheet A." (Worksheet A is reached only after Steps 1 to 5 pass; each "STOP You can't take the credit" ends the flowchart before it) The project evaluates Worksheet A line 1 on every return, nonzero on returns that STOP before Worksheet A (e.g. stage16.cleanup.mut.clwb_three_figured, investment income over $11,950, Step 2 question 2/3; generated 439, filer without a valid SSN, Step 1 question 2: line 2 3,545.00 read from it). Under the README skipped-line rule a nonzero amount (or no value) on a line the source says to skip is a defect of the side producing it, here the project. The candidate does the same. See eic.findings.md F2. Uncertainty: this treats a STOP before Worksheet A as skipping its lines.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 43, Line 27c: "Check the box on line 27c if you do not want to claim the earned income credit or if you have been instructed to check the box in the instructions for line 27a." i1040gi p. 40, Step 1, question 1: "If, in 2025: 3 or more children who have valid SSNs lived with you, is the amount on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 11b, less than $61,555 ($68,675 if married filing jointly)? ... No. STOP You can't take the credit." Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/eic.json; 1,111 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 136 partial records; 1,747 comparisons): 1,653 of 1,747 agree; 50 candidate-unknown (13 on completed returns), 35 candidate-refuses, 4 project-refuses, 5 value (all on refused returns). The candidate's conditions read eic.h_s1q1, so candidate-unknown come from its eic.h_s1q1, which compares line 11b with a limit chosen by the count of qualifying children with valid SSNs (eic.h_limit), so it needs each dependent's answers (dependent.us_half and the rest) even when line 11b is at or above the largest limit and the question is No whatever the count; the project tests that limit first (eic.below_top) and the interview does not ask those answers there. A candidate that needs answers the source does not need to determine the result is a model error (README), as in round 3. Witness: classm.f4952.1, project no, candidate unknown. The value differences are generated returns that answer married filing separately with household.married false; the candidate reads "married taxpayer whose filing status is married filing separately" from household.married, the project from the status (eic.married_rules); i1040gi p. 41, Step 3, question 3 / Step 4, question 1: "Are you a married taxpayer whose filing status is married filing separately or head of household?" -- a married-filing-separately filer is married. All are refused returns, so no box is filed (as ruled for the same reading in round 2, generated 71). Witness: generated 71 (no qualifying child, status married filing separately, household.married false, line 11b negative): project no (Step 4, question 1 "Yes. STOP You can't take the credit", no 27c instruction), candidate yes through its Worksheet B line 4b STOP; generated 239, 246, 323 and 480 are the same pattern. The candidate-refuses (dependent other_claimant and married-child gates, i1040gi p. 44) and the 4 project-refuses (Form 2555, Form 8814, sa.dependent and Step 1 question 3 gates, cited) are on refused returns: scope. Checked: the project checks 27c on the Worksheet B line 4b STOP ("If line 4b is zero or less, STOP You can't take the credit. Check the box on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 27c", i1040gi p. 47) through eligibility with line 2 of zero (stage14.eic.wsb_stop_27c expects yes). Project stands.

No. STOP You can't take the credit." Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/eic.json; 1,099 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 132 partial records; 1,731 comparisons): 1,631 of 1,731 agree; no value difference; 48 candidate-unknown (13 on completed returns), 51 candidate-refuses, 1 project-refuses. The candidate's 27c conditions read eic.h_pre and eic.h_agi_ok, so it inherits the same unknowns. The candidate-unknown come from its helper eic.h_pre, which needs the child count (for its income limit) and investment income (f1040.line2a) before the Step 1, question 1 STOP that line 11b alone decides when it is at or above the largest limit; the project tests that limit first (eic.below_top) and the interview does not ask those answers there. A candidate that needs answers the source does not need to determine the result is a model error (README). Witnesses: classm.f4952.1 (head of household, line 11b $388,706.00) project 0, candidate unknown; audit.household.hoh_married_no_community_property (completed; line 11b $120,000.00) candidate unknown (dependent eic_ssn and us_half, f1040.tax_exempt_interest, eic.qc_of_another not supplied). The 51 candidate-refuses are scope: its declared gates on eic.h_pre (sa.excluded_income, scope.other_line16) and the dependent other_claimant and married gates it reaches through the child count fire only on returns the project refuses (classm.retirement.3, classm.s179.3, classm.tcw.10). The project refusal (stage9.eic.refuse.dependent_of_another, candidate no) is the cited sa.dependent gate (i1040gi p. 42, Step 4, question 6; scope). Project stands.

No. STOP You can't take the credit." i1040gi p. 40, Step 2, question 2: "Is your investment income more than $11,950?" Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/eic.json; 1,111 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 136 partial records; 1,747 comparisons): 1,630 of 1,747 agree; no value difference; 40 candidate-unknown (8 on completed returns), 65 candidate-refuses (all on refused returns), 9 project-unknown, 3 project-refuses. The candidate-unknown come from its eic.h_s1q1, which compares line 11b with a limit chosen by the count of qualifying children with valid SSNs (eic.h_limit), so it needs each dependent's answers (dependent.us_half and the rest) even when line 11b is at or above the largest limit and the question is No whatever the count; the project tests that limit first (eic.below_top) and the interview does not ask those answers there. A candidate that needs answers the source does not need to determine the result is a model error (README), as in round 3. Witnesses: classm.f4952.1 (head of household, line 11b $388,706.00) project $0.00, candidate unknown (dependent[dep_c].us_half); classm.f4952.2 (incomplete) likewise. The candidate-refuses are its declared gates (eic.h_dep_screen: a child who is the qualifying child of another person, married, or under the divorced-parents rule; sa.excluded_income; scope.other_line16) on returns the project also refuses (classm.tcw.10, classm.carloan.1, classm.retirement.3, classm.s179.3): scope. The 3 project-refuses are cited gates (i8889 HSA screen, retirement special exceptions, sa.dependent at i1040gi p. 42, Step 4, question 6 on stage9.eic.refuse.dependent_of_another): scope. The 9 project-unknown (stage14.ho.gross_limit, audit.sa.negative_agi_medical) withhold f1040.tax_exempt_interest, part of the Step 2 investment income the interview asks of every filer; the candidate reaches $0 only because its eligibility test fails first (representation). The T-071 change (ambiguity link on eic.separated_box) does not touch this line. Project stands.

If you meet these requirements, make sure you check the box in the Dependents section that discusses the special rule for separated spouses". Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/eic.json; 1,099 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 132 partial records; 1,731 comparisons): 1,675 of 1,731 agree; no value difference; 3 candidate-unknown (1 on a completed return), 51 candidate-refuses, 2 project-refuses. The candidate now limits the box to married filers filing separately or as head of household (eic.h_married_ns), as the project does, but conditions it on eic.h_pre. The candidate-unknown come from its helper eic.h_pre, which needs the child count (for its income limit) and investment income (f1040.line2a) before the Step 1, question 1 STOP that line 11b alone decides when it is at or above the largest limit; the project tests that limit first (eic.below_top) and the interview does not ask those answers there. A candidate that needs answers the source does not need to determine the result is a model error (README). Witnesses: classm.f4952.1 (head of household, line 11b $388,706.00) project 0, candidate unknown; audit.household.hoh_married_no_community_property (completed; line 11b $120,000.00) candidate unknown (dependent eic_ssn and us_half, f1040.tax_exempt_interest, eic.qc_of_another not supplied). The 51 candidate-refuses are scope: its declared gates on eic.h_pre (sa.excluded_income, scope.other_line16) and the dependent other_claimant and married gates it reaches through the child count fire only on returns the project refuses (classm.retirement.3, classm.s179.3, classm.tcw.10). The 2 project-refuses are cited gates (HSA unsupported, retirement special) on refused returns. Project stands.

Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/eic.json; 1,111 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 136 partial records; 1,747 comparisons): 1,702 of 1,747 agree; 3 candidate-unknown (1 on a completed return), 35 candidate-refuses, 4 project-refuses, 3 value. The candidate-unknown come from its eic.h_s1q1, which compares line 11b with a limit chosen by the count of qualifying children with valid SSNs (eic.h_limit), so it needs each dependent's answers (dependent.us_half and the rest) even when line 11b is at or above the largest limit and the question is No whatever the count; the project tests that limit first (eic.below_top) and the interview does not ask those answers there. A candidate that needs answers the source does not need to determine the result is a model error (README), as in round 3. Witness: audit.household.hoh_married_no_community_property (completed; line 11b $120,000.00) project no, candidate unknown (dependent[child].us_half). The value differences are generated returns that answer married filing separately with household.married false; the candidate reads "married taxpayer whose filing status is married filing separately" from household.married, the project from the status (eic.married_rules); i1040gi p. 41, Step 3, question 3 / Step 4, question 1: "Are you a married taxpayer whose filing status is married filing separately or head of household?" -- a married-filing-separately filer is married. All are refused returns, so no box is filed (as ruled for the same reading in round 2, generated 71). Witnesses: classm.eic.6 and generated 115, 415: project yes, candidate no. The refusals are on refused returns (scope). T-071 check: the change only links amb.2025.separated_spouses_box (chosen: the box is checked when the earned income credit's special rule is used, Step 3, question 6), which matches the expression and the deciding text; no value changed. Project stands.
